title: Salford Lancaster Memorial
narrative: Flight Lieutenant Lines and his crew of 106 Squadron RAF departed RAF Metheringham on 30 July 1944, tasked with attacking enemy positions at Cahagnes in Normandy. The operation was aborted before the target was reached, and Lancaster PB304 turned for home still carrying its full bomb payload. Battle damage, mechanical failure, or communications disrupted by German interference — the precise cause remains unclear — prevented a safe return, and the aircraft came down over Salford, Lancashire. All seven crew members were killed, along with two civilians on the ground. Among those lost was Sergeant Mohand Singh, the rear gunner — one of the Indian aircrew who served with the RAF during the war.

crew.name: Peter Lines
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and explosion at Regatta Street, Salford. Made two attempts to land on Littleton Road playing fields to avoid populated areas, demonstrating extraordinary bravery.
crew.bio: Pilot of Lancaster PB304 (ZN-S), 106 Squadron. His heroic attempts to avoid crashing into densely populated Salford prevented an even greater loss of civilian life.

crew.name: Raymond Barnes
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and subsequent explosion.
crew.bio: Flight engineer serving with 106 Squadron at RAF Metheringham.

crew.name: Harry Reid
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and explosion. The only Canadian in the crew.
crew.bio: Canadian navigator serving with the RCAF, the sole Canadian among the multinational crew.

crew.name: John Harvey Steel
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and explosion.

crew.name: Arthur William Young
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and explosion.
crew.bio: Wireless operator and air gunner serving with 106 Squadron.

crew.name: John Bruce Thornley Davenport
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and explosion.

crew.name: Mohand Singh
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash and explosion. One of many Indian airmen who served with the RAF during the war.
crew.bio: Indian rear gunner, representative of the significant contribution made by Indian airmen to RAF Bomber Command during WW2.

cause_of_loss: Returned from aborted Normandy operation with full bomb payload; battle damage or mechanical failure; garbled communications possibly due to German interference
operation_target: Attacking enemy positions at Cahagnes, Normandy
memorial_details:
Upright limestone tablet with black inscription. RAF Crest and motto at top centre.

Unveiling Ceremony (30th July 1994): The unveiling of the Avro Lancaster PB304 memorial in Agecroft Cemetery, Salford.
